# Code Map — Budgeting (Zero-Based Budgeting Console)

Next.js 16 / React 19, Owner/Accountant only. The design system (ui/, theme.ts,
globals.css, NavRail, HeaderClock) is a **verbatim copy of Dispatcher** — change Dispatcher
first, then re-copy; never edit the copy in place. Manifest + drift check: Budgeting/CLAUDE.md.

## Screens — Budgeting/components/screens (7 top-level)
<!-- gen:budgeting-screens:start -->
| Screen | ~Lines |
|---|---|
| ActualsVsBudget.tsx | ~200 |

| shared.tsx | ~200 |
Sub-screen folders: screens/codes/ (2), screens/periods/ (8)
<!-- gen:budgeting-screens:end -->
<!-- notes:budgeting-screens:start -->
- Every period-scoped screen (lib/nav.ts PERIOD_SCOPED — all but Settings) renders screens/periods/PeriodChooser until a period is entered (lib/workingPeriod.ts, sessionStorage); PeriodBanner's SWITCH PERIOD is the only way out, blocked while lib/periodHold.ts holds a request.
- BudgetPeriods.tsx is only a host for periods/PeriodDashboard (LifecycleStepper, PlanningChecklist, PriorityBreakdown, CopyFromPeriodPanel, one AllocationSection per code category). Headline tiles are the server's totals; the by-priority breakdown is summed client-side.
- A period is planned in exactly one place, the dashboard: the flat Allocations screen was deleted rather than fixed, so don't re-add a second entry point (the reasoning is in lib/nav.ts).
- Budget codes belong to a period (each period has its own chart); screens/codes/CopyCodesPanel copies a chart from another period.
- After a transition, item save/removal or copy, the UI polls with refetchUntil (stateAfter / itemReflects predicates) before refreshing the period list — reads are eventually consistent.
<!-- notes:budgeting-screens:end -->

- RoleGate enforces the Owner/Accountant client-side gate (UX only — the security boundary is the gateway BudgetAccess policy on /api/budgeting).
- BudgetItemFormModal adds/edits one budget item (cost build-up, priority, recurrence, spend type) — the planning unit since items replaced one set figure per code; on the wire it is still an allocation (/periods/{id}/allocations).
<!-- notes:budgeting-components:end -->

## Lib — Budgeting/lib (28 files)
<!-- gen:budgeting-lib:start -->
api/ (9): budgeting, budgeting.requests.test, budgeting.test, format, identity, identity.test, shared, transport, transport.test
Top-level: accessSeam.test, auth, claims.test, claims, clipboard, data, format, money.test, money, nav, period, periodHold, roles.test, roles, theme, types, useToday, workingPeriod.test, workingPeriod
<!-- gen:budgeting-lib:end -->
<!-- notes:budgeting-lib:start -->
- api/budgeting.ts is the real API wiring — periods, per-period codes (/periods/{id}/codes) AND budget items (/periods/{id}/allocations) come from the backend; data.ts keeps only the mock actuals/variance (plus a budgetCodes lookup feeding those mock rows).
- api/identity.ts is the one client here that calls a non-budgeting endpoint (Identity's /api/identity/auth/profile, feeding components/ProfileForm.tsx in the Settings Profile tab); its PUT sends the whole profile, so an omitted field clears rather than preserves.
<!-- notes:budgeting-lib:end -->
